context:
Archive item 1: SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
Source format: research notebook

SGS Research Notebook No. 7
Straits Genealogical Society, Singapore
Cover period: 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
Keeper: L. C. Wee, Honorary Secretary

---

**1986-03-15 (Saturday)**

Morning at the Society rooms, 2nd floor, 18 Armenian Street. Continued work on the Tan family file (File T-14). Received a photocopy of a Straits Settlements birth register page from the National Archives (NAS) – reference SS B/1888/204. The entry confirms a birth registered on 14 April 1888 for a male child named Tan Ah Kow, born 12 April 1888, father Tan Cheng Huat, mother Lim Neo, residence Middle Road. The NAS copy is clear; the original register was in fair condition, some water damage at the spine but the entry is fully legible.

In the research notebook entry dated 1986-03-15, Tan Ah Kow's birth_date is recorded as 1888-04-12. Record status: current. This is now the current entry for this individual; the earlier entry in Notebook No. 4 (dated 1982-11-02) which gave the date as 1888-04-13 is superseded. The earlier reading was based on a family Bible held by a grand-nephew, and the discrepancy was likely a transcription error in the Bible itself or a misreading of the register page. The NAS register is the more reliable source. I have noted this correction in the margin of the old entry and will inform the family association at the next meeting.

Also checked the 1900 Straits Directory (copy in our library) for Tan Cheng Huat – listed as a clerk at Guthrie & Co., address 12 Middle Road. This matches the residence given in the birth register. No other children listed for this couple in the 1888-1895 birth indexes; will need to check the baptism records at the Armenian Church for any earlier or later children.

Marginal note: Check NAS for the family's death records. The family association (Kongsi) records may have a copy of the original certificate.

Spent the afternoon sorting the Lim family correspondence. Letters from 1920s-1930s, mostly in English and Chinese. The English ones are from a brother in Penang, discussing remittances and property. The Chinese ones I cannot read – will need to ask Mrs. Goh if she can translate. Filed them in Box L-3, pending translation.

Society administration: Received notice from the Registry of Societies that our annual return is due by 31 March. Treasurer's report for the March meeting is ready; I have placed it in the file for the committee. Also, the printer has sent a proof of the new membership brochure – I will bring it to the next meeting for approval.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-16 (Sunday)**

No formal research today. Attended the morning service at the Prinsep Street Presbyterian Church, where the pastor mentioned a memorial service for a former member, Mrs. Seah Cheng Neo, who passed away in January. I made a note to check if we have her family file; I believe she may be connected to the Seah family of Kampong Glam. The church has a set of baptism and marriage registers that may be useful for other families.

Afternoon: visited the cemetery at Bukit Brown with my brother. We were looking for the grave of a possible ancestor, one Tan Kim Seng (d. 1880?), but the cemetery is very overgrown in parts. We did not find the grave, but we did locate a well-maintained plot for a Tan Boon Tat (d. 1932) – not our line, but I recorded the details in case it is useful for another researcher. The cemetery office has a map, but it is not to scale and some paths are not marked. Will need to go back with a compass and possibly a machete.

Evening: read through some notes from the 1970s on the Chua family of River Valley. The notes are in the hand of the late Mr. Tan Cheng Lock, who was our secretary from 1965 to 1974. His handwriting is difficult to read, but I have transcribed the key dates into a new sheet for the file. The Chua family line is not currently active in our research, but the file is kept for reference.
Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-18 (Wednesday)**

Visited the National Library this morning to consult the Straits Settlements records on microfilm. I was looking for any mention of Tan Ah Kow in the newspapers of the period, particularly the *Malacca Observer* and the *Straits Times*. I found nothing directly, but I did find a notice in the *Straits Times* of 15 June 1903 regarding a meeting of creditors of a firm called "Tan Ah Kow & Co., merchants, Malacca." I have copied the notice – it lists the firm's liabilities and the names of the creditors. This may or may not be our Tan Ah Kow; the name is common. I have noted the reference in the file and will investigate further if time permits.

Also at the library: consulted the *Malacca Directory* for 1905 and 1910, which lists residents and businesses. In the 1905 edition, there is a "Tan Ah Kow, merchant, 12 Heeren Street" – this matches the address in the letters from Tan Ah Seng. This is a promising lead. I have copied the relevant pages and filed them with the property correspondence.

Afternoon: back at the Society rooms. Mrs. Goh brought in a box of old photographs that belonged to her late aunt, who was a member of the Society in the 1960s. The photographs are mostly of family gatherings and outings, but there are a few that appear to be of old Malacca streetscapes. I have sorted them into an envelope and labelled it "Malacca scenes, ca. 1900-1920, from Mrs. Goh." They may be useful for the exhibition we are planning for the Society's anniversary. I will ask Mrs. Goh if she can identify any of the people in the photographs.

Received a reply from the Registry of Societies acknowledging our annual return. The Treasurer's report for the March meeting was approved at the committee meeting last week, and the minutes have been typed. The printer's proof of the new membership brochure was also approved; the final print run should be ready by the end of the month. I have placed a copy of the proof in the file.

The research notebook states that Tan Ah Kow's birth_place was Malacca, Straits Settlements. Record status: current.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-19 (Thursday)**

Spent most of the day at the Land Office in Malacca. I took the bus up early in the morning and arrived just after nine. The office is in the old government building near the square. I asked for the land records for 12 Heeren Street, but the clerk informed me that the records for the pre-war period are held in the State Archives in Kuala Lumpur, not in Malacca. He did, however, allow me to consult the current land register, which shows that the property is now owned by a company called Heeren Development Sdn. Bhd. There is no indication of the previous owners in the current register.

I then went to the Malacca State Archives, which is a short walk from the Land Office. The archives are in a converted warehouse and are quite cramped. The staff were helpful, but they told me that the pre-war land records are in the process of being microfilmed and are not yet available for public consultation. They suggested that I write to the National Archives in Kuala Lumpur to request access. I have made a note of the procedure and will draft a letter next week.

Before leaving Malacca, I walked past 12 Heeren Street. The shophouse is still standing, though it has been renovated and now houses a souvenir shop. I took a photograph for the file. It is strange to think that Tan Ah Kow, whose birth_place was Malacca, Straits Settlements, may have lived and worked in that very building. The connection is not yet proven, but the evidence is accumulating.

Back in Singapore by evening. I have filed the photograph and the notes from the Land Office in the Tan family file, under "Property – Malacca."
**1986-03-20 (Friday)**

Morning at the Society. Filed the Malacca photographs and the notes from the Land Office visit. The Tan family file is getting thick now; I have divided it into three folders: "Property – Malacca," "Correspondence," and "Certificates & Records." The third folder is nearly full, so I started a fourth, labelled "Deaths & Obituaries."

Went through the backlog of letters that came in while I was away. One from a Mr. Goh Cheng Huat of Penang, who is enquiring about the Goh family of Upper Penang Road. I have noted his address and will respond next week. Another from a Miss Lim Siew Hong, who believes her grandfather was a friend of Tan Ah Kow. She says she has a photograph of the two of them standing outside a shophouse, possibly in Malacca, taken around the 1920s. I have written back, asking her to bring the photograph to the Society or to send a copy. If it is genuine, it would be a useful addition to the file.

In the afternoon, I began transcribing the obituary notices from the *Straits Times* microfilm for the month of September 1965. This is slow work, as the microfilm reader at the National Library is old and the image is often blurred. I managed to find two relevant notices so far. The first is for a Tan Ah Kow, who died at his residence in Singapore on 23 September 1965. The obituary states that he was a native of Malacca, Straits Settlements, and that he was survived by his wife, three sons, and two daughters. The funeral was held at the Bidadari Cemetery. According to the obituary noted in the research notebook, Tan Ah Kow's death_date is 1965-09-23. Record status: current.

The second notice is for a Tan Ah Koe, who died at the General Hospital on 28 September 1965. The name is spelled differently, and the address given is a different street, so I do not think this is the same person. I have made a note of it anyway, in case the spelling error appears in other records. See entry for 1986-03-21 for further details.

I also checked the death registers for the early 1960s, but the registers are not indexed by name, only by date of registration. This makes the search very time-consuming. I will need to come back to this.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-21 (Saturday)**

At the Society for the morning. The printer's proof of the membership brochure has arrived; it looks good. I have signed off on it, and the final print run should be ready by the end of next week.

In the afternoon, I returned to the National Library to continue with the microfilm. I found another obituary, this time for a Tan Ah Koe, who died on 28 September 1965, at the age of 72. The obituary lists the deceased as a resident of 45 Smith Street, Singapore. The surname is the same, but the given name is spelled differently from our Tan Ah Kow, and the address is not one that appears in any of our records. I have noted the details in the "Deaths & Obituaries" folder, but I do not believe this is the same person. The name difference is significant, and the address does not match any of the properties associated with the Tan family.

I also found a notice for a Tan Ah Kow who died in 1963, but the age given was 58, which does not match our records. It is possible that this is a different individual, or that the age is incorrect. I have noted it as a "possible" entry and will check against other records when I have the chance.

The microfilm reader was out of order for an hour, so I spent the time reading the *Straits Times* for September 1965 on paper. The library has a bound volume for that month. I found a short article about a fire at a godown on River Valley Road, but nothing relevant to the Tan family.

I have filed the notes from today in the "Deaths & Obituaries" folder.
**1986-03-24 (Monday)**

At the Society in the morning. The new membership brochures have arrived from the printer. They look very good. I have put a stack on the front desk and sent the rest to the storage room.

I also received a letter from the National Archives of Singapore regarding our request for access to the pre-war land records. They have confirmed that we may view the records by appointment, but they ask that we limit our visits to two hours at a time, as the reading room is small. I have written back to book a slot for next Tuesday morning.

In the afternoon, I continued with the marriage indexes at the library. I finished 1909 and started on 1910. The handwriting in the indexes is quite variable; some years are very neat, but others are almost illegible. I have to be careful not to miss entries.

I found a possible match for our family: a marriage registered in June 1910 between a Tan Ah Kow and a Lim Chwee Neo. The registration number is 1910/1487. I will need to obtain a copy of the marriage certificate to confirm the details, but the names and the timeframe fit with what we know of the family.

I have noted the registration details in the "Marriages" folder.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-25 (Tuesday)**

Morning at the Society. I filed the correspondence from Mrs. Goh in the "Penang Enquiries" folder and noted her contact details in the address book.

I also had a visit from Mr. Chee, who is a member of the Society. He is researching his own family and asked whether we have any records for the Chee family from the late 19th century. I told him that we do not hold any Chee family records specifically, but I pointed him to the land records at the National Archives and the church registers at the library. He seemed pleased with the suggestions and said he would start there.

In the afternoon, I returned to the library and obtained a copy of the marriage certificate for the June 1910 marriage I found yesterday. The certificate is in good condition, and the details are clear.

From the marriage certificate, Lim Chwee Neo's marriage_date is 1910-06-05. Record status: current. The groom is listed as Tan Ah Kow, and the marriage took place in Singapore. This matches our records, and I am satisfied that this is the correct entry. I have filed the copy of the certificate in the "Marriages" folder, and I will update the family tree accordingly.

I also spent some time going through the 1911 marriage index, but I did not find any entries that match our family.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-26 (Wednesday)**

At the Society for most of the day. I updated the family tree chart with the marriage details from the certificate. The chart is now more complete for the generation that includes Tan Ah Kow and Lim Chwee Neo.

I also wrote a short summary of the findings for the Society's records, so that future researchers will have the information. The summary is in the "Marriages" folder, along with the certificate copy.

In the afternoon, I went through the "Deaths & Obituaries" folder to check the entries I have noted over the past few weeks. I want to make sure that none of the "possible" entries are actually related to our family. I looked again at the 1963 death notice for a Tan Ah Kow, aged 58. Our Tan Ah Kow would have been about 79 in 1963, so the age does not match. I have decided to mark this entry as "unlikely" and will not pursue it further.

I also checked the 1965 obituary for Tan Ah Koe. The address and the spelling of the name are both different from our records, so I am confident that this is not the same person. I have left the entry in the folder but marked it as "not related."

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-27 (Thursday)**
**SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20**

---

**1986-03-15 (Saturday)**

Morning at home – no library hours. I sorted the loose notes I had taken in the last two weeks and pinned them into the back of this notebook for later transcription. Some of these are rough copies of tombstone inscriptions from Bukit Brown, taken with the Society's camera but not yet cross-checked against the published list in the *Journal* (1931 edition). The handwriting on the older stones is very worn, so I will need to go back with chalk and a better angle of light before I can be sure of the dates.

In the afternoon, I telephoned Mrs. Gan (the Society secretary) about the microfilm order from the National Archives. She confirmed that the reels for the Straits Settlements birth registers 1880–1895 have arrived and are now available for viewing in the reading room. I will go on Monday morning to look at the 1887–1889 volumes specifically.

Also made a note to check the 1888 index for the name "Lim Chwee Neo" – I recall from the older family notes (see NB2, p. 14) that there is some question about whether her birth was registered in Singapore or in Malacca. The family bible says Malacca, but the 1931 journal entry lists Singapore. This will need to be resolved before I update the master chart.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-16 (Sunday)**

No research today. Church service in the morning, then a long lunch with my cousin Ah Huat, who is visiting from Kuala Lumpur. He mentioned that he has a box of old photographs from our grandfather's time, mostly from the 1930s, and he thinks there might be a picture of Tan Ah Kow and Lim Chwee Neo's wedding party. He promised to bring the box down next month. I told him not to worry about the condition – even a damaged photo can be useful for identifying people by their positions in the group.

I also wrote a short letter to the Malacca registry office, asking whether they hold any birth records for the period 1885–1890 that might have been transferred from the old Portuguese settlement office. I am not sure if such a transfer was ever made, but it is worth asking. I will keep a copy of the letter in the "Correspondence" folder.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-17 (Monday)**

At the National Archives from 9:30 to 12:45. The microfilm reader on table 3 is still giving trouble – the image keeps drifting out of focus – so I used table 5 instead. I went through the 1887 birth register, reel 2, page by page. The entries are in English and Jawi, and the handwriting is generally legible, though some of the clerks' names are hard to make out.

I found a possible entry for a "Lim Chwee Neo" on reel 2, frame 47. The entry is dated 1888-03-12, and the father is listed as "Lim Ah Chong, merchant, of Telok Ayer Street." However, the mother's name is recorded as "Koh Swee Neo," which I have not seen in our family notes. I have noted the full entry in the back of this notebook (see loose sheet marked "1888 birth – LC N"). This is only a *possible* match – I will need to check the Malacca records before deciding.

In the afternoon, I returned to the Society and spent an hour in the library. I looked at the 1910 *Straits Directory* to find the address of Tan Ah Kow's shop, which is listed as 12 Market Street. This matches the address given on the marriage certificate I found earlier this month. I have added this to the family file as supporting evidence.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-18 (Tuesday)**

A good day for the Tan family branch. I went to the library in the morning and found a copy of the 1911 *Singapore and Straits Directory* which lists a "Tan Ah Kow, provision merchant, 12 Market Street" – the same address as in 1910. This is a small confirmation, but it helps to establish that the family remained at that address for at least two years after the marriage.
**SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20**

---

**1986-03-19 (Wednesday)**

Went to the Society early to sort the loose sheets from yesterday before the library opened. The 1911 directory entry is now filed under Tan Ah Kow, with a cross-note on the 1910 card. I also photocopied the relevant page of the directory – the copy is a bit dark on the left margin but the address is legible. I have placed the photocopy in the Tan family folder.

At 10:00 I walked over to the cemetery on the hill behind the old school. The gate was unlocked, which was a small mercy. I spent about two hours walking the rows, looking for the Tan Ah Kow plot that an elderly cousin mentioned when I spoke to her last month. She said the stone was near the back wall, under a rain tree. I found several Tan stones but nothing that matches. One stone, badly weathered, reads "Tan Ah Kow, d. 1924" – but the surname is common and the dates do not align with what we know. I took a rubbing anyway. I will ask the cousin whether the family plot might be on the other side of the hill, where the newer graves are.

In the afternoon I went back to the National Archives. The microfilm reader on table 5 was free, so I continued with the 1888 birth register, reel 2. I found another possible entry for the Lim family – this time a "Lim Chwee Kim," born 1888-06-02, father "Lim Ah Chong, merchant." The mother is listed as "Koh Swee Neo" again. I have noted this on the loose sheet marked "1888 birth – LC N." It is curious that the mother's name appears in both entries. I must check whether "Koh Swee Neo" is a sister or a cousin of the woman we have in our records.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-20 (Thursday)**

A frustrating morning. I went to the Registrar's office at Fort Canning to look for a death certificate for Tan Ah Kow. The clerk was helpful but could not find any record under that name for the years 1920–1930. She suggested that the death might have been registered in Malacca, or that the family did not register it at all. I have written a note in the "Correspondence" folder to follow up with the Malacca office.

In the afternoon I returned to the cemetery with the rubbing from yesterday. I compared it with the cousin's description – she said the stone had a small bird carved at the top, but the one I found has no such carving. So the stone is probably not the right one. I will leave a note in the Tan family folder to mark this as *not a match*.

I also spent an hour in the Society library looking at the 1920 *Straits Directory*. Tan Ah Kow is not listed, but a "Tan Ah Koe" appears at 12 Market Street. The spelling is different, but it might be the same person. I have added a note to the family file with a question mark. I will check the 1921 directory next week.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-21 (Friday)**

Morning at the National Archives. I continued with the 1888 birth register, reel 2, and found a third entry listing "Lim Ah Chong" as father – this time for a "Lim Chwee Lian," born 1888-09-15. The mother is again "Koh Swee Neo." Three entries with the same parents in one year is not impossible, but it is worth noting. I have added this to the loose sheet.

In the afternoon I went to the Society and met with the librarian, Mrs. Tan, about the microfilm collection. She told me that the Archives has a separate reel for the 1889 register, which I had not known about. I will request it next week.

I also received a reply from the Malacca registry office. They wrote that they do not hold birth records for the period 1885–1890, and they suggest that such records might have been kept by the church. I have filed the letter in the "Correspondence" folder. The church records might be worth checking, but I am not sure which church would have served the area at that time. I will ask the Society's contact in Malacca.
**SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-24 to 1986-03-28**

---

**1986-03-24 (Monday)**

Morning at the Society. I found in the library a copy of the *Malacca Weekly Chronicle* for 1885–1886, on microfilm. I spent two hours going through the church notices column, but the paper only lists baptisms for the English and Dutch churches in town, and none of the names match the Lim family. I have made a note in the Malacca correspondence file that the church route may be a dead end, unless the family was Roman Catholic, in which case St. Peter's would be the likely parish. I will write to the parish office this week.

Mrs. Tan has put aside for me the Archives reel for the 1889 birth register. I will pick it up on Wednesday morning.

In the afternoon I helped with the Society's monthly membership meeting. The room was crowded – about forty people. The speaker was Dr. R. Menon, who talked about the Tamil community in early Singapore and the problems of tracing families who arrived as indentured labourers. He mentioned that many of the relevant registers are in the Tamil Nadu State Archives in Madras, and that microfilm copies are not yet available in Singapore. Several members asked questions about the "missing years" 1870–1880. I took notes on a loose sheet, now filed under "Talks – 1986".

*Marginal note: Dr. Menon's address is in the correspondence folder. He offered to check one name for me if I send it by post.*

---

**1986-03-25 (Tuesday)**

Morning at the Archives. I started on the 1889 birth register, reel 3. The handwriting is worse than the earlier years – the clerk seems to have used a different pen and the ink has bled through in places. I did find one entry of interest: a "Lim Chwee Kim," female, born 1889-02-11, father "Lim Ah Chong," mother "Koh Swee Neo." This is the fourth child with the same parents in the registers. I have added it to the loose sheet.

I also checked the *Straits Directory* for 1921, as promised. Tan Ah Koe is still listed at 12 Market Street, but there is no Tan Ah Kow anywhere in the directory. I am now fairly confident the two names refer to the same man, but I have left the question mark in the family file until I see a signature or a death record.

After lunch I went to the cemetery again, this time with the sexton, Mr. Goh. He showed me the older section, behind the chapel, where the stones are mostly from the 1910s and 1920s. We walked the rows for about an hour. He pointed out that many of the stones have been re-set or replaced, and that the original plots are not always where the current markers are. This explains why my earlier search did not find the Tan stone. I have marked the cemetery map with the section he showed me.

*Marginal note: Mr. Goh says the burial registers for 1915–1925 are kept at the office, not at the Archives. I should ask to see them next time.*

---

**1986-03-26 (Wednesday)**

Morning at the Archives, reel 3 again. I finished the 1889 birth register. No further entries for the Lim family. I have now gone through 1888 and 1889 completely. The loose sheet shows:

- Lim Chwee Lian, b. 1888-09-15, parents Lim Ah Chong & Koh Swee Neo
- [two further 1888 entries – see loose sheet for details]
- Lim Chwee Kim, b. 1889-02-11, same parents

I will need to decide whether these are all the same couple or whether there are two different "Lim Ah Chongs" in the district. The addresses given in the register are not always legible, but where I can read them, two of the entries give "River Valley Road" and one gives "Club Street." That suggests two different men, or one man who moved. I have written to the Land Office to ask about the 1888–1890 tenancy records for those two streets.

SGS Research Notebook No. 7
Straits Genealogical Society, Singapore
Cover period: 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
Keeper: L. C. Wee, Honorary Secretary

---

**1986-03-15 (Saturday)**

Morning at the Society rooms, 2nd floor, 18 Armenian Street. Continued work on the Tan family file (File T-14). Received a photocopy of a Straits Settlements birth register page from the National Archives (NAS) – reference SS B/1888/204. The entry confirms a birth registered on 14 April 1888 for a male child named Tan Ah Kow, born 12 April 1888, father Tan Cheng Huat, mother Lim Neo, residence Middle Road. The NAS copy is clear; the original register was in fair condition, some water damage at the spine but the entry is fully legible.

In the research notebook entry dated 1986-03-15, Tan Ah Kow's birth_date is recorded as 1888-04-12. Record status: current. This is now the current entry for this individual; the earlier entry in Notebook No. 4 (dated 1982-11-02) which gave the date as 1888-04-13 is superseded. The earlier reading was based on a family Bible held by a grand-nephew, and the discrepancy was likely a transcription error in the Bible itself or a misreading of the register page. The NAS register is the more reliable source. I have noted this correction in the margin of the old entry and will inform the family association at the next meeting.

Also checked the 1900 Straits Directory (copy in our library) for Tan Cheng Huat – listed as a clerk at Guthrie & Co., address 12 Middle Road. This matches the residence given in the birth register. No other children listed for this couple in the 1888-1895 birth indexes; will need to check the baptism records at the Armenian Church for any earlier or later children.

Marginal note: Check NAS for the family's death records. The family association (Kongsi) records may have a copy of the original certificate.

Spent the afternoon sorting the Lim family correspondence. Letters from 1920s-1930s, mostly in English and Chinese. The English ones are from a brother in Penang, discussing remittances and property. The Chinese ones I cannot read – will need to ask Mrs. Goh if she can translate. Filed them in Box L-3, pending translation.

Society administration: Received notice from the Registry of Societies that our annual return is due by 31 March. Treasurer's report for the March meeting is ready; I have placed it in the file for the committee. Also, the printer has sent a proof of the new membership brochure – I will bring it to the next meeting for approval.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-16 (Sunday)**

No formal research today. Attended the morning service at the Prinsep Street Presbyterian Church, where the pastor mentioned a memorial service for a former member, Mrs. Seah Cheng Neo, who passed away in January. I made a note to check if we have her family file; I believe she may be connected to the Seah family of Kampong Glam. The church has a set of baptism and marriage registers that may be useful for other families.

Afternoon: visited the cemetery at Bukit Brown with my brother. We were looking for the grave of a possible ancestor, one Tan Kim Seng (d. 1880?), but the cemetery is very overgrown in parts. We did not find the grave, but we did locate a well-maintained plot for a Tan Boon Tat (d. 1932) – not our line, but I recorded the details in case it is useful for another researcher. The cemetery office has a map, but it is not to scale and some paths are not marked. Will need to go back with a compass and possibly a machete.

Evening: read through some notes from the 1970s on the Chua family of River Valley. The notes are in the hand of the late Mr. Tan Cheng Lock, who was our secretary from 1965 to 1974. His handwriting is difficult to read, but I have transcribed the key dates into a new sheet for the file. The Chua family line is not currently active in our research, but the file is kept for reference.

Visited the National Library this morning to consult the Straits Settlements records on microfilm. I was looking for any mention of Tan Ah Kow in the newspapers of the period, particularly the *Malacca Observer* and the *Straits Times*. I found nothing directly, but I did find a notice in the *Straits Times* of 15 June 1903 regarding a meeting of creditors of a firm called "Tan Ah Kow & Co., merchants, Malacca." I have copied the notice – it lists the firm's liabilities and the names of the creditors. This may or may not be our Tan Ah Kow; the name is common. I have noted the reference in the file and will investigate further if time permits.

Also at the library: consulted the *Malacca Directory* for 1905 and 1910, which lists residents and businesses. In the 1905 edition, there is a "Tan Ah Kow, merchant, 12 Heeren Street" – this matches the address in the letters from Tan Ah Seng. This is a promising lead. I have copied the relevant pages and filed them with the property correspondence.

Afternoon: back at the Society rooms. Mrs. Goh brought in a box of old photographs that belonged to her late aunt, who was a member of the Society in the 1960s. The photographs are mostly of family gatherings and outings, but there are a few that appear to be of old Malacca streetscapes. I have sorted them into an envelope and labelled it "Malacca scenes, ca. 1900-1920, from Mrs. Goh." They may be useful for the exhibition we are planning for the Society's anniversary. I will ask Mrs. Goh if she can identify any of the people in the photographs.

Received a reply from the Registry of Societies acknowledging our annual return. The Treasurer's report for the March meeting was approved at the committee meeting last week, and the minutes have been typed. The printer's proof of the new membership brochure was also approved; the final print run should be ready by the end of the month. I have placed a copy of the proof in the file.

The research notebook states that Tan Ah Kow's birth_place was Malacca, Straits Settlements. Record status: current.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-19 (Thursday)**

Spent most of the day at the Land Office in Malacca. I took the bus up early in the morning and arrived just after nine. The office is in the old government building near the square. I asked for the land records for 12 Heeren Street, but the clerk informed me that the records for the pre-war period are held in the State Archives in Kuala Lumpur, not in Malacca. He did, however, allow me to consult the current land register, which shows that the property is now owned by a company called Heeren Development Sdn. Bhd. There is no indication of the previous owners in the current register.

I then went to the Malacca State Archives, which is a short walk from the Land Office. The archives are in a converted warehouse and are quite cramped. The staff were helpful, but they told me that the pre-war land records are in the process of being microfilmed and are not yet available for public consultation. They suggested that I write to the National Archives in Kuala Lumpur to request access. I have made a note of the procedure and will draft a letter next week.

Before leaving Malacca, I walked past 12 Heeren Street. The shophouse is still standing, though it has been renovated and now houses a souvenir shop. I took a photograph for the file. It is strange to think that Tan Ah Kow, whose birth_place was Malacca, Straits Settlements, may have lived and worked in that very building. The connection is not yet proven, but the evidence is accumulating.

Back in Singapore by evening. I have filed the photograph and the notes from the Land Office in the Tan family file, under "Property – Malacca."

documents.title: SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
documents.content:
**1986-03-20 (Friday)**

Morning at the Society. Filed the Malacca photographs and the notes from the Land Office visit. The Tan family file is getting thick now; I have divided it into three folders: "Property – Malacca," "Correspondence," and "Certificates & Records." The third folder is nearly full, so I started a fourth, labelled "Deaths & Obituaries."

Went through the backlog of letters that came in while I was away. One from a Mr. Goh Cheng Huat of Penang, who is enquiring about the Goh family of Upper Penang Road. I have noted his address and will respond next week. Another from a Miss Lim Siew Hong, who believes her grandfather was a friend of Tan Ah Kow. She says she has a photograph of the two of them standing outside a shophouse, possibly in Malacca, taken around the 1920s. I have written back, asking her to bring the photograph to the Society or to send a copy. If it is genuine, it would be a useful addition to the file.

In the afternoon, I began transcribing the obituary notices from the *Straits Times* microfilm for the month of September 1965. This is slow work, as the microfilm reader at the National Library is old and the image is often blurred. I managed to find two relevant notices so far. The first is for a Tan Ah Kow, who died at his residence in Singapore on 23 September 1965. The obituary states that he was a native of Malacca, Straits Settlements, and that he was survived by his wife, three sons, and two daughters. The funeral was held at the Bidadari Cemetery. According to the obituary noted in the research notebook, Tan Ah Kow's death_date is 1965-09-23. Record status: current.

The second notice is for a Tan Ah Koe, who died at the General Hospital on 28 September 1965. The name is spelled differently, and the address given is a different street, so I do not think this is the same person. I have made a note of it anyway, in case the spelling error appears in other records. See entry for 1986-03-21 for further details.

I also checked the death registers for the early 1960s, but the registers are not indexed by name, only by date of registration. This makes the search very time-consuming. I will need to come back to this.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-21 (Saturday)**

At the Society for the morning. The printer's proof of the membership brochure has arrived; it looks good. I have signed off on it, and the final print run should be ready by the end of next week.

In the afternoon, I returned to the National Library to continue with the microfilm. I found another obituary, this time for a Tan Ah Koe, who died on 28 September 1965, at the age of 72. The obituary lists the deceased as a resident of 45 Smith Street, Singapore. The surname is the same, but the given name is spelled differently from our Tan Ah Kow, and the address is not one that appears in any of our records. I have noted the details in the "Deaths & Obituaries" folder, but I do not believe this is the same person. The name difference is significant, and the address does not match any of the properties associated with the Tan family.

I also found a notice for a Tan Ah Kow who died in 1963, but the age given was 58, which does not match our records. It is possible that this is a different individual, or that the age is incorrect. I have noted it as a "possible" entry and will check against other records when I have the chance.

The microfilm reader was out of order for an hour, so I spent the time reading the *Straits Times* for September 1965 on paper. The library has a bound volume for that month. I found a short article about a fire at a godown on River Valley Road, but nothing relevant to the Tan family.

I have filed the notes from today in the "Deaths & Obituaries" folder.

documents.title: SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
documents.content:
**1986-03-24 (Monday)**

At the Society in the morning. The new membership brochures have arrived from the printer. They look very good. I have put a stack on the front desk and sent the rest to the storage room.

I also received a letter from the National Archives of Singapore regarding our request for access to the pre-war land records. They have confirmed that we may view the records by appointment, but they ask that we limit our visits to two hours at a time, as the reading room is small. I have written back to book a slot for next Tuesday morning.

In the afternoon, I continued with the marriage indexes at the library. I finished 1909 and started on 1910. The handwriting in the indexes is quite variable; some years are very neat, but others are almost illegible. I have to be careful not to miss entries.

I found a possible match for our family: a marriage registered in June 1910 between a Tan Ah Kow and a Lim Chwee Neo. The registration number is 1910/1487. I will need to obtain a copy of the marriage certificate to confirm the details, but the names and the timeframe fit with what we know of the family.

I have noted the registration details in the "Marriages" folder.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-25 (Tuesday)**

Morning at the Society. I filed the correspondence from Mrs. Goh in the "Penang Enquiries" folder and noted her contact details in the address book.

I also had a visit from Mr. Chee, who is a member of the Society. He is researching his own family and asked whether we have any records for the Chee family from the late 19th century. I told him that we do not hold any Chee family records specifically, but I pointed him to the land records at the National Archives and the church registers at the library. He seemed pleased with the suggestions and said he would start there.

In the afternoon, I returned to the library and obtained a copy of the marriage certificate for the June 1910 marriage I found yesterday. The certificate is in good condition, and the details are clear.

From the marriage certificate, Lim Chwee Neo's marriage_date is 1910-06-05. Record status: current. The groom is listed as Tan Ah Kow, and the marriage took place in Singapore. This matches our records, and I am satisfied that this is the correct entry. I have filed the copy of the certificate in the "Marriages" folder, and I will update the family tree accordingly.

I also spent some time going through the 1911 marriage index, but I did not find any entries that match our family.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-26 (Wednesday)**

At the Society for most of the day. I updated the family tree chart with the marriage details from the certificate. The chart is now more complete for the generation that includes Tan Ah Kow and Lim Chwee Neo.

I also wrote a short summary of the findings for the Society's records, so that future researchers will have the information. The summary is in the "Marriages" folder, along with the certificate copy.

In the afternoon, I went through the "Deaths & Obituaries" folder to check the entries I have noted over the past few weeks. I want to make sure that none of the "possible" entries are actually related to our family. I looked again at the 1963 death notice for a Tan Ah Kow, aged 58. Our Tan Ah Kow would have been about 79 in 1963, so the age does not match. I have decided to mark this entry as "unlikely" and will not pursue it further.

I also checked the 1965 obituary for Tan Ah Koe. The address and the spelling of the name are both different from our records, so I am confident that this is not the same person. I have left the entry in the folder but marked it as "not related."

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-27 (Thursday)**

documents.title: SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
documents.content:
**SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20**

---

**1986-03-15 (Saturday)**

Morning at home – no library hours. I sorted the loose notes I had taken in the last two weeks and pinned them into the back of this notebook for later transcription. Some of these are rough copies of tombstone inscriptions from Bukit Brown, taken with the Society's camera but not yet cross-checked against the published list in the *Journal* (1931 edition). The handwriting on the older stones is very worn, so I will need to go back with chalk and a better angle of light before I can be sure of the dates.

In the afternoon, I telephoned Mrs. Gan (the Society secretary) about the microfilm order from the National Archives. She confirmed that the reels for the Straits Settlements birth registers 1880–1895 have arrived and are now available for viewing in the reading room. I will go on Monday morning to look at the 1887–1889 volumes specifically.

Also made a note to check the 1888 index for the name "Lim Chwee Neo" – I recall from the older family notes (see NB2, p. 14) that there is some question about whether her birth was registered in Singapore or in Malacca. The family bible says Malacca, but the 1931 journal entry lists Singapore. This will need to be resolved before I update the master chart.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-16 (Sunday)**

No research today. Church service in the morning, then a long lunch with my cousin Ah Huat, who is visiting from Kuala Lumpur. He mentioned that he has a box of old photographs from our grandfather's time, mostly from the 1930s, and he thinks there might be a picture of Tan Ah Kow and Lim Chwee Neo's wedding party. He promised to bring the box down next month. I told him not to worry about the condition – even a damaged photo can be useful for identifying people by their positions in the group.

I also wrote a short letter to the Malacca registry office, asking whether they hold any birth records for the period 1885–1890 that might have been transferred from the old Portuguese settlement office. I am not sure if such a transfer was ever made, but it is worth asking. I will keep a copy of the letter in the "Correspondence" folder.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-17 (Monday)**

At the National Archives from 9:30 to 12:45. The microfilm reader on table 3 is still giving trouble – the image keeps drifting out of focus – so I used table 5 instead. I went through the 1887 birth register, reel 2, page by page. The entries are in English and Jawi, and the handwriting is generally legible, though some of the clerks' names are hard to make out.

I found a possible entry for a "Lim Chwee Neo" on reel 2, frame 47. The entry is dated 1888-03-12, and the father is listed as "Lim Ah Chong, merchant, of Telok Ayer Street." However, the mother's name is recorded as "Koh Swee Neo," which I have not seen in our family notes. I have noted the full entry in the back of this notebook (see loose sheet marked "1888 birth – LC N"). This is only a *possible* match – I will need to check the Malacca records before deciding.

In the afternoon, I returned to the Society and spent an hour in the library. I looked at the 1910 *Straits Directory* to find the address of Tan Ah Kow's shop, which is listed as 12 Market Street. This matches the address given on the marriage certificate I found earlier this month. I have added this to the family file as supporting evidence.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-18 (Tuesday)**

A good day for the Tan family branch. I went to the library in the morning and found a copy of the 1911 *Singapore and Straits Directory* which lists a "Tan Ah Kow, provision merchant, 12 Market Street" – the same address as in 1910. This is a small confirmation, but it helps to establish that the family remained at that address for at least two years after the marriage.

documents.title: SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
documents.content:
**SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20**

---

**1986-03-19 (Wednesday)**

Went to the Society early to sort the loose sheets from yesterday before the library opened. The 1911 directory entry is now filed under Tan Ah Kow, with a cross-note on the 1910 card. I also photocopied the relevant page of the directory – the copy is a bit dark on the left margin but the address is legible. I have placed the photocopy in the Tan family folder.

At 10:00 I walked over to the cemetery on the hill behind the old school. The gate was unlocked, which was a small mercy. I spent about two hours walking the rows, looking for the Tan Ah Kow plot that an elderly cousin mentioned when I spoke to her last month. She said the stone was near the back wall, under a rain tree. I found several Tan stones but nothing that matches. One stone, badly weathered, reads "Tan Ah Kow, d. 1924" – but the surname is common and the dates do not align with what we know. I took a rubbing anyway. I will ask the cousin whether the family plot might be on the other side of the hill, where the newer graves are.

In the afternoon I went back to the National Archives. The microfilm reader on table 5 was free, so I continued with the 1888 birth register, reel 2. I found another possible entry for the Lim family – this time a "Lim Chwee Kim," born 1888-06-02, father "Lim Ah Chong, merchant." The mother is listed as "Koh Swee Neo" again. I have noted this on the loose sheet marked "1888 birth – LC N." It is curious that the mother's name appears in both entries. I must check whether "Koh Swee Neo" is a sister or a cousin of the woman we have in our records.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-20 (Thursday)**

A frustrating morning. I went to the Registrar's office at Fort Canning to look for a death certificate for Tan Ah Kow. The clerk was helpful but could not find any record under that name for the years 1920–1930. She suggested that the death might have been registered in Malacca, or that the family did not register it at all. I have written a note in the "Correspondence" folder to follow up with the Malacca office.

In the afternoon I returned to the cemetery with the rubbing from yesterday. I compared it with the cousin's description – she said the stone had a small bird carved at the top, but the one I found has no such carving. So the stone is probably not the right one. I will leave a note in the Tan family folder to mark this as *not a match*.

I also spent an hour in the Society library looking at the 1920 *Straits Directory*. Tan Ah Kow is not listed, but a "Tan Ah Koe" appears at 12 Market Street. The spelling is different, but it might be the same person. I have added a note to the family file with a question mark. I will check the 1921 directory next week.

Signed, L. C. Wee

---

**1986-03-21 (Friday)**

Morning at the National Archives. I continued with the 1888 birth register, reel 2, and found a third entry listing "Lim Ah Chong" as father – this time for a "Lim Chwee Lian," born 1888-09-15. The mother is again "Koh Swee Neo." Three entries with the same parents in one year is not impossible, but it is worth noting. I have added this to the loose sheet.

In the afternoon I went to the Society and met with the librarian, Mrs. Tan, about the microfilm collection. She told me that the Archives has a separate reel for the 1889 register, which I had not known about. I will request it next week.

I also received a reply from the Malacca registry office. They wrote that they do not hold birth records for the period 1885–1890, and they suggest that such records might have been kept by the church. I have filed the letter in the "Correspondence" folder. The church records might be worth checking, but I am not sure which church would have served the area at that time. I will ask the Society's contact in Malacca.

documents.title: SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-15 to 1986-03-20
documents.content:
**SGS Research Notebook No. 7 – Entries 1986-03-24 to 1986-03-28**

---

**1986-03-24 (Monday)**

Morning at the Society. I found in the library a copy of the *Malacca Weekly Chronicle* for 1885–1886, on microfilm. I spent two hours going through the church notices column, but the paper only lists baptisms for the English and Dutch churches in town, and none of the names match the Lim family. I have made a note in the Malacca correspondence file that the church route may be a dead end, unless the family was Roman Catholic, in which case St. Peter's would be the likely parish. I will write to the parish office this week.

Mrs. Tan has put aside for me the Archives reel for the 1889 birth register. I will pick it up on Wednesday morning.

In the afternoon I helped with the Society's monthly membership meeting. The room was crowded – about forty people. The speaker was Dr. R. Menon, who talked about the Tamil community in early Singapore and the problems of tracing families who arrived as indentured labourers. He mentioned that many of the relevant registers are in the Tamil Nadu State Archives in Madras, and that microfilm copies are not yet available in Singapore. Several members asked questions about the "missing years" 1870–1880. I took notes on a loose sheet, now filed under "Talks – 1986".

*Marginal note: Dr. Menon's address is in the correspondence folder. He offered to check one name for me if I send it by post.*

---

**1986-03-25 (Tuesday)**

Morning at the Archives. I started on the 1889 birth register, reel 3. The handwriting is worse than the earlier years – the clerk seems to have used a different pen and the ink has bled through in places. I did find one entry of interest: a "Lim Chwee Kim," female, born 1889-02-11, father "Lim Ah Chong," mother "Koh Swee Neo." This is the fourth child with the same parents in the registers. I have added it to the loose sheet.

I also checked the *Straits Directory* for 1921, as promised. Tan Ah Koe is still listed at 12 Market Street, but there is no Tan Ah Kow anywhere in the directory. I am now fairly confident the two names refer to the same man, but I have left the question mark in the family file until I see a signature or a death record.

After lunch I went to the cemetery again, this time with the sexton, Mr. Goh. He showed me the older section, behind the chapel, where the stones are mostly from the 1910s and 1920s. We walked the rows for about an hour. He pointed out that many of the stones have been re-set or replaced, and that the original plots are not always where the current markers are. This explains why my earlier search did not find the Tan stone. I have marked the cemetery map with the section he showed me.

*Marginal note: Mr. Goh says the burial registers for 1915–1925 are kept at the office, not at the Archives. I should ask to see them next time.*

---

**1986-03-26 (Wednesday)**

Morning at the Archives, reel 3 again. I finished the 1889 birth register. No further entries for the Lim family. I have now gone through 1888 and 1889 completely. The loose sheet shows:

- Lim Chwee Lian, b. 1888-09-15, parents Lim Ah Chong & Koh Swee Neo
- [two further 1888 entries – see loose sheet for details]
- Lim Chwee Kim, b. 1889-02-11, same parents

I will need to decide whether these are all the same couple or whether there are two different "Lim Ah Chongs" in the district. The addresses given in the register are not always legible, but where I can read them, two of the entries give "River Valley Road" and one gives "Club Street." That suggests two different men, or one man who moved. I have written to the Land Office to ask about the 1888–1890 tenancy records for those two streets.

**5.1 Expected vs. Observed Haplogroups**

Based on the genealogical records and the patrilineal descent pattern, all male
members in this chain should share the same Y-chromosome haplogroup. The
following table compares the expected haplogroup (derived from the family record)
with the observed haplogroup from this run.

**Interpretation:** The observed haplogroups for the two sampled generations
are consistent with the expected haplogroup derived from the genealogical chain.
There is no evidence of a non-paternal event (NPE) between Generation 3 and
Generation 5 based on this marker set.

**5.2 Relationship Confirmation**

The Y-chromosome results support the documented relationship between the
samples. The SGS Instrument Run Summary 2024-03 indicates that its analysis_date
is 2024-03-18. The genetic data from this run confirms that Tan Boon Leng is the
Great-great-grandson of Tan Ah Koe, as documented in the family records. This
relationship is supported by the shared Y-haplogroup (O-M122) and the matching
Y-STR profiles obtained during pre-screening (see Section 3.2 of this report).

The chain is considered verified for the purposes of this study. The probability
of a random match for the combined Y-STR profile is less than 1 in 10,000 in the
relevant reference population (see Section 6.1 below).

---

The SGS Instrument Run Summary 2024-03 indicates that its analysis_date is 2024-03-18. Record status: current.

**6. POPULATION COMPARISON**

**6.1 Reference Population Data**

The observed haplogroup frequencies were compared against published data for
reference populations relevant to the client's reported ancestry (Fujian,
Southern China). The following table shows the approximate frequency of each
observed haplogroup in the reference population.

| Haplogroup | Frequency in Southern Chinese (Han) | Frequency in Southeast Asian (Malay/Indonesian) | Notes |
|------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|-------|
| O-M122 | 35-45% | 15-25% | Most common in Han Chinese |
| O-M95 | 5-10% | 25-35% | Common in Austroasiatic speakers |
| C-M130 | 5-10% | 5-15% | Widespread in East Asia |

These frequencies are taken from published literature (e.g., Yan et al. 2014,
Karmin et al. 2015) and are provided for context only. They are not part of the
formal analysis for this run.

**6.2 Sample Comparison**

For each sample, the observed haplogroup is consistent with the expected
population of origin based on client-provided family history.

- **SGS-2024-0318-01 (Tan Kian Huat):** O-M122. Consistent with reported
  Fujian Han ancestry.
- **SGS-2024-0318-02:** O-M95. This sample was submitted as part of a separate
  study on Malay genealogy. The haplogroup is consistent with the expected
  population.
- **SGS-2024-0318-03:** O-M122. Submitted as a control sample from a known
  Fujian Han individual. Haplogroup matches expectation.
- **SGS-2024-0318-04:** C-M130. Submitted for a study on indigenous Taiwanese
  populations. Haplogroup is consistent with published data for that group.
- **SGS-2024-0318-05:** O-M95. Part of the Malay genealogy study (same as
  SGS-2024-0318-02).
- **SGS-2024-0318-06 (Tan Boon Leng):** O-M122. Consistent with the
  genealogical chain and with the Fujian Han ancestry reported by the client.
